newsitem.title: UK: Pharmacia & Upjohn Q3 hit by currencies.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn Q3 hit by currencies.

text.p: U.S.-Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn confirmed on Thursday that currency fluctuations hurt its performance in the third quarter of the year.

The newly-merged group reported a drop in earnings per share to 39 cents from 44 cents a year earlier, after an exceptional charge of 5 cents per share for restructuring and merger costs. Net earnings fell to $204 million from $231 million.
The weaker performance was flagged by the company three weeks ago, leading analysts to cut their forecasts for the rest of the year and for 1997.

Third-quarter sales grew by a sluggish two percent to $1.7 billion. In a statement, Pharmacia & Upjohn said an unfavourable foreign exchange rate against the U.S. dollar adversely affected its reported sales increase by two percentage points.
"Principally the weakened Japanese yen affected sales and the strengthening of the Swedish krona and Italian lira increased costs in dollar terms," it said.
For the first nine months of the year, earnings per share were 6.0 percent higher at $1.39 cents before restructuring and mergers charges of 75 cents per share.

President and chief executive John Zabriskie said the company's long-term merger targets, including its aim of achieving operating profit margins of 25 percent by 1998, had not changed, with product launches and merger cost savings on schedule.

"Pharmacia & Upjohn is on track to achieve annual cost savings of $500 million by 1998, with 85 percent of that in effect by 1997." He said job cuts are ahead of schedule with 3,300 staff leaving by the end of the third quarter.
The company said the launch of cancer drug Camptosar and glaucoma dug Xalatan both boosted the third quarter performance.
But it added that pressure on the price and sales of its older products continued to constrain overall sales growth.

Sales of consumer healthcare products rose by 27 percent to $169 million in the third quarter, led by strong growth from Nicorette anti-smoking products which were boosted by a build-up in stocks prior to its over-the-counter launch in the U.S.
Sales of nutritional products fell nearly 30 percent to $68 million in the quarter, while sales of infectious disease products were down 22 percent to $118 million.
